authors: Zirui Guo, Xubin Ren, Lingrui Xu, Jiahao Zhang, Chao Huang

panels.headline: Addressing the gap in multimodal information processing
content: RAG extends LLMs by dynamically retrieving and incorporating external knowledge.
Real-world documents are multimodal, containing text, visuals, tables, and expressions.
Current RAG frameworks are limited to textual content, leading to information loss.

panels.headline: Challenges in multimodal RAG
content: Existing systems struggle with rich multimodal information.
Critical insights are often encoded in non-textual formats.
Three main technical challenges: unified representation, structure-aware decomposition, and cross-modal retrieval.

panels.headline: Dual-graph construction for multimodal RAG
content: Introduces a dual-graph strategy to integrate multimodal content and textual semantics.
Employs advanced multimodal encoders to capture intra-modal and inter-modal dependencies.
panels.figure_caption: Overview of our proposed universal RAG framework RAG-Anything.

panels.headline: Comprehensive experiments on DocBench and MMLongBench
content: Conducted experiments on two challenging multimodal benchmarks: DocBench and MMLongBench.
Evaluated across diverse domains to validate the framework's effectiveness.
panels.figure_caption: Document type distribution and statistics for the DocBench benchmark.

panels.headline: Accuracy 87.8% on DocBench, outperforming state-of-the-art methods
content: Achieved superior performance on challenging multimodal benchmarks.
Significant gains on long-context documents with multiple modalities and sections.
panels.figure_caption: Accuracy (%) on DocBench Dataset. Performance results with best scores highlighted in dark blue and second-best in light blue.

panels.headline: Effective localization and disambiguation in complex layouts
content: Correctly identified cluster separation patterns from the style-space panel.
Navigated financial tables to locate specific intersections amid similar entries.
panels.figure_caption: Multi-panel figure interpretation case. The query requires identifying cluster separation patterns from the style-space panel, while avoiding confusion from the adjacent content-space panel.

panels.headline: New paradigm for multimodal knowledge access
content: RAG-Anything addresses the limitations of text-only RAG systems.
The framework is open-sourced for further research and real-world applications.
Demonstrates significant improvements in handling long-context and complex multimodal materials.
